t.2.13.1: Having spent that night, the brāhmaṇas, masters of the Vedas, came to the royal audience hall together with the king's priests.
t.2.13.2: The ministers, the chiefs of the army, and those who were the leaders of the merchant guild, rejoicing, assembled for the purpose of Rāghava's consecration.
t.2.13.3: When the spotless sun had risen and the day of Puṣya had arrived, all was made ready by the foremost of the twice-born for the consecration of Rāma.
t.2.13.4: There are golden water jars and a well-adorned auspicious throne, and Rāma, duly furnished with a gleaming tiger skin spread out for him.
t.2.13.5: Water has been brought from the holy confluence of the Gaṅgā and the Yamunā, and from whatever other sacred rivers there are, and from pools, wells and lakes.
t.2.13.6: Streams that flow eastward, streams that flow upward, and streams that flow crosswise have been brought together, and water has been fetched from those rivers and from the oceans on every side.
t.2.13.8: Rāma's excellent yak-tail fan stands ready, white and adorned with jewels, resembling the spreading rays of the moon.
t.2.13.7: Honey, curd and ghee, parched grain, darbha grass, flowers and milk are ready, and pots of gold and silver shine there, holding parched grain, covered with the leaves of milky-sapped trees, adorned with lotuses and water lilies, and filled with the finest water.
t.2.13.9: And a white parasol, resembling the disc of the moon, stands ready, radiant and splendid, set foremost for the consecration.
t.2.13.10: The white bull stands ready, the white horse is well placed, and the splendid royal elephant, streaming with ichor, waits in attendance.
t.2.13.11: And eight auspicious maidens adorned with every ornament, and all the musical instruments, and likewise other bards as well.
t.2.13.12: Just as the consecration of the Ikṣvākus to kingship ought to be prepared, so, taking up everything of that kind, make ready the consecration of the prince.
t.2.13.13: Having assembled there at the king's command, and not seeing the lord of the earth, they said, "Who, then, will announce us to the king?"
t.2.13.14: We do not see the king, yet the sun has risen, and the consecration of the wise Rāma as heir-apparent stands ready.
t.2.13.15: While they were speaking thus, Sumantra, honored by the king, said this to all those sovereign lords of the earth.
t.2.13.16: Here I am, at the word of the king who has just awakened, asking after the well-being of you long-lived ones, and what the reason for your coming is.
t.2.13.17: Having spoken thus, he who was versed in the ancient lore came to the door of the inner apartments and praised Rāghava with blessings rich in noble qualities.
t.2.13.19: The brāhmaṇas, the chief commanders of the army and the merchants have come, O king, and they long to see you. Awaken, O Rāghava!
t.2.13.18: The blessed night has passed, and the auspicious day has arrived. Awake, O tiger among kings, and do what must be done next.
t.2.13.20: Then the king, awakening, spoke these words to the charioteer Sumantra, skilled in counsel, who was at that time praising him.
t.2.13.21: "I am not asleep at all; let him quickly bring Rāghava here." Thus King Daśaratha once again instructed the charioteer there.
t.2.13.22: Having heard the king's words and honored him with a bow of his head, he went out from the king's residence, deeming it a matter of great joy.
t.2.13.23: Having reached the royal highway, adorned with banners and flags, the charioteer heard there the talk that was all about Rāma.
t.2.13.24: Then Sumantra beheld the beautiful dwelling of Rāma, whose radiance was like that of Kailāsa and equal in splendour to the palace of Śakra.
t.2.13.25: The palace, shut by great doors and adorned with hundreds of terraces, with golden statues set prominently at its front and arched gateways of jewels and coral.
t.2.13.26: the dwelling, resembling a dense mass of autumn clouds, radiant like a cavern of Mount Meru, and adorned with very large garlands of the finest flowers.
t.2.13.27: The charioteer, in his chariot yoked with horses, gazed upon the royal palace thronged with people; then, having reached that great and richly endowed abode, the charioteer's hair bristled with delight.
t.2.13.28: Unhindered, the charioteer entered that palace, which resembled mountain peaks, immovable hills and clouds, and held clusters of great towered pavilions and splendid mansions, as a makara enters the ocean abounding in jewels.
